notes: lens: over-strictness. 64 checks. counts {"OVERSTRICT":20,"CONFIRMED":39,"MISCLASSIFIED":5}. Three structural defects account for 17 of the 20 OVERSTRICT verdicts. (1) EVM-hardcoded ADDRESS_RE on payTo — confirms vault-3rb9y and its v1 sibling: 7 of 8 payTo forms taken verbatim from the spec pack (Solana, Sui, Aptos, Stellar, XRPL, NEAR, and the spec-named role constant "merchant") grade F; the same hardcoding makes V2_EXTRA_EIP712/V1_EXTRA_EIP712 demand an EIP-712 domain from chains and mechanisms (SVM exact, EVM permit2, EVM erc7710, batch-settlement) that have none. (2) isV1Attempt() classifies ANY body carrying x402Version as a v1 attempt, so a v2 seller that echoes its own envelope into the 402 body — legal, since transports-v2/http.md puts response bodies outside the protocol — runs the whole v1 cascade and grades F on five checks. (3) the DUAL_* family compares v1 accepts[0] with v2 accepts[0], so a multi-offer seller who lists the same offers in a different order grades F; @x402/core's default selector is accepts[0] PER VERSION, which is exactly why the two arrays may legitimately differ in order. Calibration probes: the spec's own canonical 402 (transports-v2/http.md) grades C; bazaar.md's own GET example draws a warn for an object-valued output.example; the Cloudflare batch-settlement profile (cloudflare:402 + payTo "merchant") grades F on two core checks. Two counter-findings outside my lens, reported for the merge: V2_MAX_TIMEOUT and V1_MAX_TIMEOUT are warns for a field that is Required in both spec tables and non-optional in @x402/core's zod schemas (probed: safeParse fails without it) — those are understrict, filed as MISCLASSIFIED. json-schema.js is NOT over-strict: 13 legal schema shapes plus bazaar.md's examples and the CDP-validated toolshed pair all validate clean.
